summary: The common-base checksum guard authenticates exact regular-file population using bounded relative repository paths. Arch archive basenames can include a literal colon for a version epoch, as represented by the source contract fixture conmon-1:2.2.1-1-x86_64.pkg.tar.zst and its detached signature. A safe basename allowlist that excludes colon can reject an otherwise byte-bound package population before the package transaction. Admit literal colon inside the same single basename while continuing to reject traversal, control characters, non-regular inputs, incomplete/extra/duplicate checksum rows and byte drift. Preserve repository filenames and package bytes; renaming packages or rewriting repository metadata is not a path-validation repair. Corresponding maintained input consumers must use the same basename contract and the exact updated Containerfile pin. Passing these inert controls proves supplied-file coverage and path handling, not authentic transaction closure, image build, runtime custody, provisioning or publication.
title: Preserve Arch version epochs in authenticated archive filenames
